recognize_zh: 兩格各有一顆嗜中性球，核分成六到七個分葉、以細絲相連，細胞大小與顆粒大致正常，數得出 ≥6 葉即為過度分葉嗜中性球。
features: Two neutrophils (one per panel), each with 6-7 discrete nuclear lobes connected by thin chromatin strands
Dense, clumped mature chromatin; no nucleoli
Cell size only mildly enlarged; pale pink cytoplasm with fine neutrophilic granules
No toxic granulation, Dohle bodies or vacuoles
Background red cells normocytic without obvious macro-ovalocytes; rouleaux-like overlap in thick areas
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear, shown as two high-power panels, contains neutrophils with six to seven nuclear lobes joined by fine chromatin filaments. The cytoplasm is pale with normal fine granulation, and there is no toxic granulation or vacuolation. The accompanying red cells in these fields do not show conspicuous macro-ovalocytosis. Findings are consistent with neutrophil hypersegmentation, a nonspecific finding that raises megaloblastic anemia but also occurs with iron deficiency, myeloid neoplasms including myeloproliferative neoplasms, hydroxyurea and G-CSF.

ddx.vs: Megaloblastic states show hypersegmentation together with macro-ovalocytes, high MCV and low B12/folate, which must be excluded by red cell indices and vitamin levels.
Botryoid neutrophils have rounded lobes clustered radially around a central clearing, in hyperthermia, rather than a linear chain of lobes.
The rare inherited form is lifelong and familial with otherwise normal counts, whereas acquired hypersegmentation tracks with a nutritional, drug or neoplastic cause.
